findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State where the OSS survey and prior-ticket constraints are recorded (e.g. this plan's Context, an ADR, or the closing PR description) so AC5 is deterministically checkable.
evidence: 'recorded' has no named destination (ticket comment, plan doc, ADR, PR description)
Without a stated artifact location the proving check is ambiguous
findings.finding: AC5 requires that prior-ticket constraints and at least three OSS projects be 'recorded' but does not state WHERE the record lives, so an executor cannot deterministically prove the criterion in-session.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria line 'Prior ticket constraints and at least three maintained OSS projects are recorded.'
scenarios: Reviewer cannot locate the survey to confirm the three OSS references
findings.suggested_fix: Amend AC5 to name the artifact, e.g. 'recorded in the closing PR description / an ADR committed to the repo'.

search_files for 'blob:none' / 'partial-clone' shows partial-clone-related tests in at least five distinct files across tests/unit and tests/integration, not one.
The mapping is itself a plan deliverable, so the vagueness is acknowledged rather than hidden — but no candidate file is named as an anchor.
findings.finding: The plan's edit set is stated abstractly ('map each partial-clone test', 'prototype isolated small fixtures') and never names the concrete test file(s) it will touch, yet partial-clone tests are spread across several files (tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py, tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone_workflows.py, tests/unit/test_snapshot_blobless_747f.py, tests/integration/test_reclaim_bridge_history.py, tests/integration/test_prepare_reclaim_backup.py), so the blast radius of the fixture split cannot be bounded from the plan text.
findings.location: Plan > Plan (first bullet: 'Map each partial-clone test ...')
scenarios: An implementer must decide whether the fixture split touches only tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py (the cinderlike-weariful-angora fixture) or also the blobless/reclaim tests that exercise blob:none.
A reviewer cannot confirm the large-contrast guard AC (line 1) is preserved without knowing which file(s) hold the frozen tests.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Files/Scope line listing the fixture file under experiment (tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py) and explicitly mark the other blob:none-touching tests as out of scope, so 'each partial-clone test' resolves to an enumerable set.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the relevance bar for the OSS survey: each recorded project must show how it runs real Git protocol server fixtures (git daemon / upload-pack, not file:// or in-process libgit2) under parallel/xdist worker isolation, and note whether it shares or isolates the server per worker.
evidence: Plan: 'Compare fixture setup, call time, macOS wall, and aggregate runner cost; survey maintained Git-heavy OSS suites.'
AC5: 'Prior ticket constraints and at least three maintained OSS projects are recorded.'

Context: 'Shared mutable servers may create races and cross-worker contamination, and no maintained-OSS consensus has yet been established.' — the open question is precisely how OSS handles per-worker isolation of real Git servers, yet the survey criterion does not require the recorded projects to speak to that.

ABSENCE: no criterion states the recorded OSS suites must demonstrate real Git protocol (daemon/upload-pack) fixtures under parallel/xdist worker isolation, so a count of three could be met with irrelevant examples.
findings.finding: The plan commits to surveying and recording 'at least three maintained OSS projects' but sets no relevance criterion tying that prior art to the specific novel/risky combination being adopted — a real Git protocol server fixture that is isolated per concurrent (xdist) worker — so the survey could be satisfied by Git-heavy suites that never address worker-isolated real-server fixtures and thus would not ground the architecture actually being chosen.
findings.location: Plan bullet 5 ('survey maintained Git-heavy OSS suites') and Acceptance Criteria line 5 ('at least three maintained OSS projects are recorded')
scenarios: The three recorded OSS projects use in-process libgit2/dulwich or file:// URLs and never spin per-worker real Git daemons, leaving the actual concurrency/isolation decision ungrounded.
A reviewer later asks whether shared-vs-per-worker real servers is the maintained-OSS norm and finds the survey does not answer it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a step that measures the duplication-driven cost of the single existing fixture under a session/worker-group scope (built once, shared read-only) and compares it against the small-per-case-fixture split, so the chosen approach is shown at-least-as-good on the actual cost driver.
evidence: Context: 'duplicated per xdist worker'
Context: 'A possible split is to retain one exact large-object guard and use a small real Git server/repository for protocol-only cases.'
current fixture is scope="module" (tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py:63), so duplication is per-module-per-worker and re-scoping is a real lever
Plan bullet 3: 'Prototype isolated small fixtures only for cases whose failure oracle is independent of repository size'
findings.finding: The plan does not evaluate the structurally simpler alternative of eliminating the per-worker DUPLICATION cost (e.g. re-scoping the single existing fixture to session scope and/or an xdist worker-group so it is built once, read-only, and shared) before committing to building many new small per-case fixtures. The census attributes the ~32.69 s partly to the fixture being 'duplicated per xdist worker', which a scope/grouping change targets directly without adding new fixtures or new mutation-equivalence proofs.
scenarios: The measured cost is dominated by rebuilding the same fixture in each worker rather than by its object size, in which case shrinking fixtures yields far less than re-scoping/sharing.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the create-and-retire lifecycle for each per-worker fixture (fixture-scoped teardown of server processes, ports, and temp repos) and add a criterion or step asserting cleanup.
evidence: Plan mandates isolation ('do not share mutable state across workers') and AC3 forbids sharing, but neither the plan steps nor ACs specify who tears down each per-worker server/repo or a cleanup path
A small real Git server started per worker is stateful infra whose lifecycle (create/consume/retire) is otherwise unaddressed
findings.finding: The plan introduces isolated per-worker small Git servers/repositories but does not define their teardown/cleanup (RETIRE) path, risking leaked processes, ports, or temp directories accumulating across a run.
findings.location: Plan bullet 'Prototype isolated small fixtures only for cases whose failure oracle is independent of repository size; do not share mutable state across workers.' / AC3
scenarios: A worker crashes mid-test leaving a Git daemon process or lock file behind
Temp repos accumulate across repeated CI runs, filling disk
findings.suggested_fix: Use pytest fixture teardown (yield + cleanup) scoped per worker to stop the Git server and remove its temp repo; add an AC that no fixture-created process/temp dir survives the session.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether small isolated fixtures reuse/parameterize the existing `ticket_server` daemon fixture (tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py) or stand up new server scaffolding, and justify a fresh implementation if chosen.
evidence: tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py:64 already defines a module-scoped `ticket_server` fixture with git daemon startup, loopback port reservation, 30s connect retry, and terminate()+kill() cleanup
search_files shows the git-daemon pattern exists in exactly one place; no shared helper module encapsulates it
The existing fixture is production test code (not under docs/experiments/ or *_poc.*), so per FP7 this is an extend-vs-rebuild question, not an asserted rebuild
findings.finding: The plan's 'Prototype isolated small fixtures ... a small real Git server/repository' does not say whether it reuses the existing git-daemon+bare-repo fixture scaffolding or builds fresh server setup, risking duplication of daemon lifecycle/port-reservation/cleanup logic.
findings.location: Plan section 'Plan', bullet 3 ('Prototype isolated small fixtures only for cases whose failure oracle is independent of repository size')
scenarios: The small-fixture prototype re-implements git daemon startup/cleanup instead of parameterizing the existing `ticket_server` fixture (e.g., a `blob_size` argument), doubling the daemon-management surface to maintain.

Mitigating: this figure motivates the split rather than excluding work, and AC 'Before/after macOS wall and runner savings are measured' re-measures it, so it is not a silent scope-exclusion
findings.finding: The Context claim 'The integration census attributes about 32.69 worker-phase seconds to partial-clone fixtures' is a confident numeric measurement with no cited source; grepping the repo and docs for '32.69', 'worker-phase', and 'census' finds no artifact that establishes it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State a positive rationale for the small-per-case-fixture direction (e.g. why a size-independent oracle makes a small isolated fixture the right unit) so the experiment has an explicit hypothesis rather than framing it as an open 'possible split'.
evidence: Context: 'A possible split is to retain one exact large-object guard...'
Context: 'no maintained-OSS consensus has yet been established'
ABSENCE: no sentence gives an affirmative 'we choose small per-case fixtures because X' rationale tying the mechanism to the size-independent oracle property
findings.finding: The plan states motivations (cost, avoid cross-worker races) but never states a POSITIVE rationale for why prototyping small per-case real-Git fixtures is the preferred mechanism; the Context frames it as merely 'a possible split' and concedes 'no maintained-OSS consensus has yet been established', leaving the chosen direction unjustified as written.
scenarios: Implementer must choose between re-scoping, sharing, or splitting and has no stated principle to decide.
